question: Using Section 9E.12 and Figure 9E-12, state the minimum bicycle-box length, required pavement symbol, turn-on-red rule, and green-pavement coverage rule.
model_answer: Direct Answer: Under Section 9E.12, a bicycle box must be at least 10 feet long (measured from the upstream edge nearest the motor-vehicle stop line to the downstream edge nearest the crosswalk/intersection) and must contain at least one bicycle symbol marking. Turns on red are prohibited from any lane where a bicycle box is placed. Green-colored pavement is optional in a bicycle box, but if it is used it must cover the full limits of the box (and bicycle boxes are among the only applications where green pavement is permitted). Standards (mandatory): - "If used, the distance from the upstream edge of the bicycle box that is nearest to the stop line for motor vehicles to the downstream edge of the bicycle box that is nearest the crosswalk or intersection shall be at least 10 feet. At least one bicycle symbol marking (see Figure 9E-12) shall be used in the bicycle box." - "Turns on red shall be prohibited from the lane where a bicycle box is placed." (shown in the full-page view of Section 9E.12) - "If used, green-colored pavement shall be used in the full limits of the bicycle box." (shown in the full-page view accompanying Figure 9E-12, Sheet 1) - "If used, green-colored pavement shall be limited to: … D. Two-stage bicycle turn boxes (see Section 9E.11), E. Bicycle Boxes (see Section 9E.12), and F. As a background for bicycle detector symbols (see Section 9E.15)." Options (permitted): - "A bicycle box (see Figure 9E-12) may be used to increase the visibility of stopped bicycles on the approach to a signalized intersection during the portion of the signal cycle when a red signal indication is being displayed to motor vehicles in the approach lane(s) that is behind the box." - "Green-colored pavement may be used in a bicycle box." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 9E-12 (Sheet 1 of 2) shows a bicycle box across one lane with the "10 ft MIN." dimension between the intersection stop line and the advance stop line, bicycle symbol markings inside the box, and optional green-colored pavement filling the full box. - [Image 2] Figure 9E-12 (Sheet 2 of 2) shows a bicycle box across multiple lanes with a NO TURN ON RED (R10-11) sign, the "10 ft MIN." dimension, and required countdown pedestrian signals. - [Image 3] The full-page view of Section 9E.12 contains the Standard provisions, including "Turns on red shall be prohibited from the lane where a bicycle box is placed." - [Image 4] The full-page view with Figure 9E-12 Sheet 1 contains Standard §13: "If used, green-colored pavement shall be used in the full limits of the bicycle box." - [Image 5] The full-page view of Section 3H.06 lists Bicycle Boxes (Section 9E.12) among the permitted applications of green-colored pavement. Citations: - Section 9E.12 Standard §6 (p.1105) - Section 9E.12 Option §1 (p.1105) - Section 9E.12 Option §12 (p.1106) - Section 3H.06 Standard §2 (p.626) - Figure 9E-12 (p.1106) - Page 1146 - Page 1147 - Page 1148 - Page 666
gold_answer: The bicycle box must be at least 10 feet long, include at least one bicycle symbol, prohibit turns on red from its lane, and, if green pavement is used, fill the entire limits of the box.
